claims.text: Chromium surface doping applied by thermal diffusion will form a continuous chromium-rich oxide barrier on boride-based component surfaces.
A chromium-rich oxide barrier will improve the resistance of boride-based components to molten-aluminum corrosion.
Standard boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment lack specialized surface modifications.
A low concentration of chromium can be introduced at the surface of boride components through a controlled thermal diffusion process.
The treatment should remain effective at approximately 660°C to 750°C.
Optimized chromium content will form a uniform oxide layer without impairing the underlying boride structure.
The chromium treatment will produce a coherent and adherent chromium oxide layer associated with the boride matrix.
The chromium oxide layer will resist attack by molten aluminum.
Chromium atoms diffuse to the surface during thermal treatment.
Surface chromium oxidizes to form a dense chromium oxide layer.
The dense chromium oxide layer acts as a physical and chemical barrier to molten aluminum.
The barrier slows the interfacial reaction between molten aluminum and the boride-based component.
Slowing the interfacial reaction reduces molten-aluminum corrosion.
Chromium-doped samples should exhibit lower weight loss than untreated boride-based samples after molten-aluminum exposure.
Chromium-doped samples should preserve microstructural integrity better than untreated samples during a typical service interval.
The protective effect depends on formation of a uniformly distributed chromium oxide layer.
Non-uniform doping or deviations in the thermal treatment may negate the protective effect.
Operation beyond the designed temperature range may negate the protective effect.
Chromium may interact with the boride matrix in ways that compromise mechanical properties.
The current evidence pool contains no direct experimental evidence that chromium doping improves molten-aluminum corrosion resistance in boride-based systems.
